Baseline construction

Comparable period: same day-of-week + same daypart + same location

Window: rolling 8-week window

Recency weighting: last 4 weeks 60% · weeks 5–8 40%

Outlier exclusion: shifts where revenue > 2 standard deviations from mean are excluded

Formulas
RPLHnet_revenue_in_window / total_labor_hours_in_window DET
Productivity Score(RPLH_current / RPLH_baseline) × 100 DET
Overstaffing Est.MAX(0, actual_hours − (net_revenue / target_RPLH)) EST
Est. Labor Cost Reductionexcess_hours × estimated_fully_loaded_wage EST
Labor Variance $(RPLH_baseline − RPLH_current) × actual_hours (diagnostic)
Labor Cost %total_wages / net_revenue × 100

B. Formula trace
Contribution Margin per item
CM = unit_price_at_sale − food_cost_per_unit

Total CM
Total CM = CM per item × units sold

Weighted Avg CM
Weighted Avg CM = SUM(CM × units) ÷ SUM(units)

Mix Shift
Mix Shift = current weighted avg CM − 8-week baseline weighted avg CM

Estimated Exposure
ABS(mix shift) × total items sold

B2. Weighted CM Reconciliation

Displayed matrix shows top 9 dinner items. 273 other mapped dinner items are included in weighted average CM.

Target total CM
2,004 × $8.42 = $16,873.68

Top 9 visible CM
≈ $14,545.40 (sum of itemized Total CM in table)

Other mapped dinner items

CM/item ≈ $2,328.28 ÷ 273 ≈ $8.53

Conclusion
This reconciles the visible item table to the 2,004-item weighted average of $8.42.
C. Classification logic

Menu engineering · 2×2 classification:

  • Popularity threshold = 8.0%
  • CM threshold = $8.75 (set above weighted avg $8.42 so above-average alone is not sufficient for Star classification)
  • Star = high popularity + high CM
  • Plowhorse = high popularity + low CM
  • Puzzle = low popularity + high CM
  • Dog = low popularity + low CM

Current distribution (top 9 dinner items):

  • Stars: 2 — Spicy Vodka Pasta, Espresso Martini
  • Plowhorses: 3 — Crispy Chicken Sandwich, Burger, Truffle Fries (Watch)
  • Puzzles: 2 — Mushroom Risotto, Burrata Toast
  • Dogs: 2 — Beet Salad, Kids Pasta

Truffle Fries is classified Plowhorse · Watch (near-threshold Plowhorse) — its CM ($7.60) sits below the $8.75 threshold and its popularity (15.8%) is above 8.0%. Operationally lower risk than Crispy/Burger because fries may drive attachment/guest satisfaction, but strict threshold logic still applies.

Plowhorse share of dinner volume: Primary Plowhorses (Crispy + Burger) = 613 / 2,004 = 30.6%. Including Truffle Fries Watch = 930 / 2,004 = 46.4%.

D. Food cost precedence

SKC resolves food cost using this order:

  1. Inventory integration actual (real-time COGS)
  2. Manual SKC recipe config
  3. Category default percentage (heuristic, labeled)
  4. Suppressed / unavailable

Current demo: recipe cost file is stale 18d, so CM is shown ESTIMATED and verification is blocked.

F. Data quality rules
  • Missing food cost → category default only if configured · label [HEURISTIC]
  • Stale food cost → reduce confidence and block verified savings
  • Items with fewer than 5 units sold → insufficient data, excluded
  • LTO / seasonal items under 6 weeks → excluded from long-run baseline, not classified as Dog
  • Price change >10% mid-period → split pre/post analysis
  • Negative CM → validation prompt and exclude from weighted avg until operator review
  • Always use price at time of sale for historical analysis
G. Output type labels
  • CM/item: deterministic if actual food cost current · estimated if recipe cost stale · heuristic if category default
  • Classification: deterministic from thresholds · confidence inherits cost-data quality
  • Mix shift: estimated
  • Exposure: estimated · not verified
  • Simulation: simulated · not verified
  • Verified Savings: only after monitoring + guardrails pass + recipe costs fresh
H. LLM restrictions

LLM provides narrative only. It cannot:

  • Compute CM
  • Change item classification
  • Invent food costs
  • Remove estimated labels
  • Call simulated value verified
  • Call active recovery saved
  • Override Data Quality blockers
  • Recommend owner approval without disclosing stale cost data

Action Evidence
Status rules, verification logic, guardrails, and workflow definitions. This page defines how actions move between Pending, Active Recovery, Ready to Verify, Blocked, and Verified — and what blocks each transition.
Status definitions
PENDINGAwaiting decision
ASSIGNEDOwner assigned, not implemented
IMPLEMENTEDOperating change in place, day 0
MONITORINGIn window, guardrails tracked
READYWindow complete, guardrails pass
VERIFIEDIn ROI Proof, counted
BLOCKEDCannot proceed (DQ/approval)
REJECTEDOperator declined
Verification logic

An action moves to VERIFIED only when all of the following hold:

1. Monitoring window complete (default 28 days · category-specific).
2. All guardrails hold for the full window — no breaches.
3. Source data is fresh (no stale-source confidence penalty active).
4. Owner review/sign-off completed in ROI Proof.

Until all 4 conditions are met, the action's value is [ACTIVE RECOVERY] or [ESTIMATED] — never counted as Verified Savings.

Guardrails (default)
Labor — Ticket time must not worsen. Guest sentiment must not drop. Sales/throughput must not fall.
Menu — Unit decline ≤ 7%. Sentiment stable. Refund rate stable.
Table Turns — Avg check stable. Sentiment stable. Faster turns not counted if either degrades.
Manager override — Allowed at any point. Override pauses the monitoring window; reset on resume.
Financial label rules
[ESTIMATED]Pre-implementation projection
[SIMULATED]Modeled lift, not yet attempted
[ACTIVE RECOVERY]Tracking in monitoring window
[VERIFIED]Counted in ROI Proof
[BLOCKED]Excluded from all counts

Every dollar value carries time basis, output type, and a derivation link to evidence. Never "saved" or "recovered" until all 4 verification conditions hold.

Workflow transitions
Detected (Profit Recovery) → Pending Pending + Operator approval → Assigned Assigned + Implemented → Monitoring Monitoring (window complete + guardrails OK) → Ready Ready + Owner verification → Verified (ROI Proof) Any state + DQ failure or approval gate → Blocked Any state + Guardrail breach → Reverted / Failed
LLM restrictions

Claude (Sonnet) generates action recommendations and rationale, but is not permitted to:

— Set status to Verified. Verification is rule-driven, not LLM-driven.
— Override guardrails. Manager override only.
— Call estimated/simulated values "saved" or "recovered" in any output.
— Skip the monitoring window or shorten it without operator approval.

All financial outputs are decision-support only; the operator is the final authority.

Peer benchmark: P25 small-multi independents on Toast in the East Bay (n=42 locations · last 90 days). Update cadence: quarterly.
Threshold rules
RPLH floor: $36.50/hr. Below this, the service is flagged as a labor productivity leak signal. Floor is recalibrated quarterly against peer P25.
Labor % ceiling: 31.0%. Above this, labor cost is flagged as outside target band. Target is restaurant-specific (full-service casual dining, no delivery).
Minimum sample: 4 comparable services in the trailing window. Fewer = no detection. Prevents single-service noise from generating false leaks.
Daypart normalization: RPLH is always compared to same-daypart baseline. Tuesday lunch RPLH is not compared to Saturday dinner RPLH.
Confidence floor: Below 60% source confidence, no detection is generated. Source confidence reflects POS sync freshness and 7shifts token state.
Server Coaching
Three-axis server analysis from Toast POS data, peer-group normalized (same daypart × section × location). Identifies patterns — triple-threats, revenue specialists, hospitality specialists, coaching opportunities — not flat rankings. Outputs are [ESTIMATED].
⚠
Coaching-only. These analyses reflect server-attributable patterns from Toast POS and are intended for coaching, training, and recognition. Per SKC Terms of Service, this data may not be used as the sole input for scheduling, promotion, discipline, or termination decisions. Tip percentage is deliberately not used as a metric — it correlates with section assignment and party demographics, not service quality.

Methodology
Three independent axes per server: Revenue (premium attach, items/check, modifier capture), Retention (repeat-guest rate, requires loyalty), Reliability (comp/void/complaint rate). Peer groups: same daypart × section × location. Min sample: 12 shifts in trailing 60d. Min peer group: 3 servers.
Surfaced vs hidden
Servers analyzed14

Servers without top/bottom quartile signal are not surfaced — coaching effort produces no meaningful lift, and surfacing them invites misuse.
Doctrine Server Coaching diagnoses patterns. Turn coaching opportunities into actions — the lifecycle lives in Actions. Recognition and shadow-training are operator-led, not auto-actioned. Verified savings only after coaching changes are implemented and revenue lift is measured against guardrails (avg check stable, sentiment stable).
Labor Evidence
Formulas, sources, confidence rules, data-quality blockers, and LLM restrictions. This page defines how labor leaks are detected and what blocks verification.
Formula trace
RPLH = Net sales ÷ labor hours Excess hours = scheduled − required Required = covers ÷ covers-per-server target Weekly $ = excess hrs × loaded wage × services/wk Loaded wage = base + tax + WC + benefits Monthly run-rate = weekly × 4.33

RPLH is diagnostic only. Dollar recovery is computed from excess hours × loaded wage, not from RPLH directly.

Source health
Toast POS · connected · live
Sales by daypart · connected
7shifts · token stale 18h
Baseline window · 8 weeks
Wage assumptions · operator-confirmed

Stale 7shifts reduces confidence from 85% to 78%. Refresh token to restore.

Confidence rules
Floor for detection60%
Floor for action70%
Floor for verification80%
Stale 7shifts penalty−7 pts
Stale POS penalty−12 pts
Missing wage data−15 pts

Confidence is a function of source freshness, sample size, and pattern strength. Below 70% = pending only, no auto-action.

Guardrails (verification-side)
Ticket time must not worsen during monitoring window. Measured per service vs baseline.
Guest sentiment must not drop. Tracked via review platforms + complaint patterns.
Sales / throughput must not fall. If covers drop >5% with staffing held constant, guardrail trips.
Manager override allowed at any point. Pauses monitoring window; resumes on resume.

Staffing reduction is not counted as verified if service quality degrades, even if labor cost dropped.

Data-quality blockers
POS down > 6h → detection paused for affected period.
7shifts stale > 24h → detection continues but confidence reduced.
Wage data unconfirmed → dollar values labeled [ESTIMATED · WAGE UNCONFIRMED]; cannot move to action.
Sample < 4 services → no detection generated.

All current blockers visible in Data Quality.

Server Coaching methodology

Primary metric: Premium item attach rate.

Attach % = checks w/ premium tag ÷ total checks

Secondary metrics: items/check, modifier capture, comp rate.

Peer group:

Same daypart × section type × location. Min 3 peer servers required.

Sample floor:

12+ shifts in trailing 60 days per server. Below floor = no ranking.

Surfaced output:

Top quartile (assets) + bottom quartile (opportunities). Middle 50% intentionally hidden — not actionable as coaching targets.

Deliberately excluded:

Tip percentage. Correlates with section assignment and party demographics, not service quality. Including it would generate structurally biased rankings.
Total tips, total sales. Confounded by section, daypart, party size. Not server-attributable.
Composite "performance score". Hides what's being measured. Each metric stays decomposable.
Server Coaching · use restrictions

Per SKC Terms of Service, Server Coaching outputs may not be used as the sole input for:

— Scheduling decisions (which servers get which shifts)
— Promotion or demotion decisions
— Disciplinary action
— Termination

Allowed use cases:

— Coaching conversations and training
— Shadow training pairing (top performer + new hire)
— Recognition and morale
— Identifying section/daypart structural issues

Final personnel decisions remain with the operator. SKC data is one input among many.

LLM restrictions

Claude (Sonnet) generates labor analysis and natural-language summaries, but is not permitted to:

— Set or modify confidence scores. Confidence is rule-driven.
— Override RPLH thresholds or wage assumptions.
— Call estimated values "saved" or "recovered" in any output.
— Auto-create actions. Operator approval required.
— Generate language about a server's character, attitude, or perceived motivation. Only measurable behavior in metrics.
— Compare servers across different peer groups. Daypart/section/location must match.

LLM outputs are decision-support only. Final authority is the operator.

When SKC is wrong
Confident wrongness is the fastest way to lose operator trust. SKC must have a surface for being told it was wrong — and a behavior change when it learns it was.
3 surfaces
A · Reverification A verified action can be reopened
Risotto removal
Verified $97/wk · 4 weeks ago · Berkeley menu cleanup
Verified
Guardrails will re-evaluate against the last 4 weeks of data. If guardrails now fail, the line is removed from Verified Savings and the value reverts.
B · Pattern-of-rejection alert SKC reduces its own confidence when a category is repeatedly rejected
Labor recommendations · 2 of last 5 rejected by operator
SKC reducing labor detection confidence for this account by 10%. New labor recommendations will require manager review before surfacing.
40% rejection rate
Triggers when more than 30% of recommendations in a category have been rejected. Rejected reasons are stored in Operating Memory and used to recalibrate the detector.
C · Dispute a verification A previously verified line can be flagged as wrong
Tuesday lunch labor adjustment
Verified $42/wk · 8 weeks ago · Oakland
Verified
Why are you disputing this verification?
Disputed verifications are flagged for human review. The $/mo run-rate associated with the line is not retroactively removed from ROI without review — but it stops contributing to subscription-coverage math until reviewed.
Doctrine: SKC must surface its own wrongness, change behavior in response, and never quietly delete history. Reverification, pattern-of-rejection alerts, and dispute escalation are the three surfaces where this happens. Operators are explicitly empowered to tell SKC it was wrong.

How SKC works · what's automated, what's rules-based, what's AI
SKC is positioned as an "AI Restaurant Profit Manager." Here is exactly what that means — and what it doesn't mean.
▾
Automated · deterministic Computed by SKC from your data — no model judgment involved
  • Detection thresholds (e.g. "CM gap > 10 pts for 3+ weeks")
  • Guardrail monitoring (every service · pass/fail against limits)
  • Source freshness tracking (Toast, 7shifts, KDS, Recipe Cost, Reviews, Accounting)
  • Baseline calculation (rolling windows · weighted averages · anomaly exclusion)
  • Lost-cover math (seat-based capacity model)
  • Time-basis arithmetic (per-service → weekly → monthly run-rate)
Rules-based · logic SKC executes Deterministic decision rules — not learned, not adaptive without an explicit update
  • Recommendation ranking (by weekly exposure × confidence)
  • Action sequencing (which leak to surface first today)
  • Blocker resolution order (which DQ failure to ask the operator to fix first)
  • Verification eligibility (which monitoring windows can close into Verified Savings)
  • Approval-required gating (e.g. price changes >5% require owner sign-off)
  • FOH-action lockout when kitchen root cause is unconfirmed
AI-assisted · LLM-generated narrative only An LLM writes the words. It does not compute the numbers.
  • Evidence drawer explanatory text (the prose around the numbers)
  • "Ask SKC" responses (cite the rules engine output; never invent figures)
  • Weekly digest narrative wording (numbers plug in from the rules engine)
  • Operator memo phrasing (do this / don't change / watch / reverse if)
Doctrine: every dollar value on SKC is computed by deterministic rules, not generated by an LLM. AI is a language layer over the rules engine — it explains numbers, it never produces them. If the rules engine cannot compute a number, no narrative is generated; the surface stays empty until the rules can fire.
Why this loop improves retention Doctrine
Verified value creates renewal proof. Push digest creates habit without requiring login. GM scorecard creates internal adoption. Human value review prevents silent churn. Operating memory creates legitimate switching cost. Quarterly detectors expand value surface area.

View 15-min line review playbook
  1. Arrive at Berkeley 30 min before Friday lunch (typically 10:30 AM)
  2. Walk each kitchen station — check mise en place and prep completeness
  3. Identify handoff friction between expo, grill, and sauté positions
  4. Implement one targeted process change before service starts
  5. Watch KDS ticket times during service — target ≤ 12 min
  6. Log findings in SKC → Throughput for baseline comparison
  7. Repeat for 3 consecutive Fridays to confirm fix holds

Formula trace
Theoretical turns (4 hrs × 60 min) ÷ 76 min target = 3.16 turns/seat
Actual turns (4 hrs × 60 min) ÷ 94 min actual = 2.55 turns/seat
Turn deficit 3.16 − 2.55 = 0.61 turns/seat
Theoretical lost covers 0.61 × 42 seats = 25 covers/service
Realization haircut × 36% (East Bay full-service casual)
Lost covers/service floor(25 × 0.36) = 9
Avg check $76 (Fri dinner trailing 4-week)
Revenue / service 9 × $76 = $684
Weekly ~$680 (1 Fri service / week · floored)
Monthly run-rate $680 × 4.33 = ~$2,944/mo
Floor rule: lost covers floor(), never ceil(). Realization haircut applied before flooring.
Why 36% realization? Not every theoretical seat-turn converts to an actual cover. Walk-ins peak in specific windows; not all of the "freed time" lands in a peak window. Realization haircut is operator-configurable; 36% reflects East Bay full-service casual benchmark for Friday dinner.

Table Turn Evidence
Formulas, filters, exclusions, mode definitions (KDS vs Proxy), and LLM restrictions. This page defines how table-turn opportunities are detected and what blocks verification.
Formula trace
Theoretical turns = svc hrs × 60 ÷ target Actual turns = svc hrs × 60 ÷ actual Turn deficit = theoretical − actual Lost covers = floor(deficit × seats × haircut) Revenue / svc = lost covers × avg check Monthly = weekly × 4.33

Lost covers always floored, never rounded up. Realization haircut applied before flooring.

Filters & exclusions
DINE_IN only. TAKE_OUT and DELIVERY do not have meaningful dining duration and are excluded entirely.
Voided checks excluded. Voids don't represent real cover throughput.
Still-open checks excluded from closed-period analysis. Open-check duration is meaningless until the check closes.
Comped services excluded from avg-check baseline. Comps distort revenue/cover.

All exclusions are enforced before duration math runs. Filter state is visible in the legacy Stage Flow filter bar.

KDS vs Proxy mode
KDS MODE · default. Kitchen Display System provides stage timing (Seat→Order, Order→Food, Food→Dessert, Dessert→Check). Stage decomposition active.
PROXY MODE · KDS data missing. Total duration only (seat → close), no stage decomposition. Outputs labeled [PROXY] / [HEURISTIC].

Proxy mode is a data quality state, not a separate destination. Mode auto-switches based on KDS feed availability.

Guardrails (verification-side)
Avg check must not drop during monitoring window. Per-cover spend tracked per service.
Guest sentiment must not worsen. Tracked via review platforms + complaint patterns.
Complaints / 100 covers must not rise. Front-line rushing signal.
Manager override allowed at any point. Pauses monitoring window.

Faster turns are not counted as verified recovery if check or sentiment degrades — even if covers/service improved.

Confidence rules
Floor for detection60%
Floor for action70%
Floor for verification80%
Proxy mode penalty−15 pts
KDS partial penalty−8 pts
Sample < 4 servicesNo detection

Confidence reflects KDS feed health, sample size, and pattern strength. Proxy mode is workable but capped.

LLM restrictions

Claude (Sonnet) generates stage-level analysis and natural-language summaries, but is not permitted to:

— Override realization haircut or seat capacity.
— Round lost covers up. Floor rule is hard.
— Call estimated revenue "saved" or "recovered" in any output.
— Suppress Proxy/Heuristic labels when KDS data is unavailable.

LLM outputs are decision-support only. Final authority is the operator.

Review Turn Playbook
Friday dinner closeout playbook
Affected service

Oakland · Friday Dinner · 7–9 PM peak window

Recommendation: Deploy handheld closeout + check-drop script.

Exact steps
  1. Pre-assign two handhelds to closing servers before 7 PM.
  2. Drop check within 2 minutes after entrée clear.
  3. Offer handheld payment at the table before guests ask.
  4. Manager checks POS open-check aging every 20 minutes.
  5. Escalate tables open > 90 minutes only if guest pace allows.
Staff script
"Whenever you're ready, I can close this out right here so you don't have to wait."
What not to do
  • Do not rush guests before they finish.
  • Do not pressure dessert or drink decisions.
  • Do not reduce hospitality to hit turn targets.
  • Do not count recovery if avg check or sentiment worsens.
  • Do not treat estimated opportunity as verified ROI.
Guardrails
  • Avg check must not fall more than 5%.
  • Guest sentiment on service speed must not worsen.
  • Individual server avg check must remain stable.
  • Review comments mentioning "rushed" trigger manager review.
  • Recovered covers only count after guardrails hold for full monitoring window.

B. Seat-based capacity formula
Per-check dining duration
duration = closed_at − opened_at
Duration overage
overage = avg_current − avg_baseline = 74 − 63 = +11 min
Seat-based lost covers
lost_covers = floor(
  ((SP / baseline) − (SP / current))
  × seat_count
  × effective_fill_factor
)
Numeric trace · Friday dinner
(180 / 63) = 2.8571
(180 / 74) = 2.4324
difference = 0.4247

0.4247 × 38 seats × 0.56 fill = 9.04
floor(9.04) = 9 covers / wk
Revenue opportunity
9 × $75.50 = $679.50 → displayed as ~$680 / wk [ESTIMATED — not guaranteed recoverable revenue]
C. Why no avg-party-size multiplier

Seats already represent cover capacity, so avg party size is not multiplied into the seat-based model. Each freed seat-minute is treated as one potential cover-minute. Multiplying by party size on top of seat count would double-count: a single 4-top doesn't gain four new "seat-units" when the table opens — it gains one table-turn worth of seats.

What effective_fill_factor represents: the share of theoretical added capacity expected to convert into actual guest covers during observed demand. For this daypart it reflects historical waitlist + walk-in conversion behavior for Friday dinner at Oakland. It collapses what some models split into separate "utilization" and "demand-fill" parameters into one auditable input.

J. False-win logic

Primary metric: dining duration should decrease.

A faster table is not a win if:

  • Avg check drops more than 5%.
  • Guest sentiment / review sentiment worsens.
  • Server avg check falls.
  • Rushed-service comments increase.

If avg check drops, net impact is recalculated as (covers_gained × new_avg_check) minus revenue lost to lower check size.

K. LLM restrictions

LLM narrative may explain the data but cannot:

  • Change formulas or model inputs
  • Remove the [ESTIMATED] label
  • Claim guaranteed recoverable revenue
  • Round lost covers up
  • Invent KDS stages
  • Include TAKE_OUT or DELIVERY in duration logic
  • Treat active recovery as verified ROI
